election._note: Elected 17 April 2024 for a four-year term, so constitutionally due by spring 2028; no date announced. The game books November 2027 -- flagged as earlier than the statutory latest. The real system elects by preferential list in ten constituencies with a 5% per-constituency bar plus diaspora and minority seats; the machinery's national list is the nearest reading. Wikipedia, 'Next Croatian parliamentary election'.

dissolution._note: Arts. 104 and 112: the Sabor can topple the Prime Minister, and if it then fails to elect a successor within 30 days the Government falls and the President, on the Government's proposal with the Prime Minister's countersignature, dissolves the Sabor -- the machinery's confidence_failure, reachable only through a lost confidence vote. Elections follow within 60 days, which is the two-month notice; the Sabor cannot be dissolved during a state of war (Art. 82). Ustav RH, Arts. 82, 104 and 112.

head_of_state._note: The President, directly elected for five years by two-round vote; last elected January 2025 (second round), so the next is due by January 2030 -- the game books the likely first round of December 2029. Commander-in-chief in peacetime and co-responsible for foreign policy on paper; in practice a cohabitation problem rather than an executive. Wikipedia, 'President of Croatia'.
head_of_state.title: President

amendment._note: Art. 137: the Sabor adopts constitutional amendments by a two-thirds majority of all deputies, after the procedure of Arts. 136 -- a revision committee whose conclusions bind the final text. The template's two_thirds is the real bar, no translation needed. Ustav RH, Arts. 136-137.
amendment._referendum_note: Art. 87 lets the President call a referendum on a proposed constitutional amendment and Art. 136 lets the Sabor route one through the same stage, but no amendment content in this game prices a Croatian popular vote -- SVK.json's reason. Croatia's one constitutional referendum (EU accession, 2012) ran on its own statute.
amendment._permits_system_change_note: No written eternity clause; the 1990 founding and three decades of practice treat the democratic republic as beyond ordinary revision -- AUT.json's thinner citation, flagged as convention rather than a written clause.

judicial._note: Ustavni sud Republike Hrvatske, Arts. 128-141: decides on the conformity of laws with the Constitution, on competence disputes and on the President's impeachment. Ustav RH, Arts. 128-141.

formation._note: The President gives the mandate to a designated candidate, who presents the Government and its programme to the Sabor and must win its confidence within 15 days -- an investiture in the machinery's vocabulary. Censure of the Prime Minister carries by a majority of ALL deputies and is CONSTRUCTIVE -- the same vote must elect a successor -- which the template's simple_present reads coarsely; recorded here rather than detuned, SVK.json's tolerance of an absolute-of-all reality behind the permitted reading. Ustav RH, Arts. 97, 110-111.

government._pretender_note: Whom data/laws/amendments.json's Restoration Act puts on the throne. Authored per nation because the law is generic and the dynasty is not; a monarchy points this at its own sitting monarch.

fiscal._note: General government, IMF/OECD estimates ~2024, rounded, on the same conventions as SVK.json's block. VAT 25% is the statutory standard rate; corporate 18% is the statutory rate (10% for small firms, blended up to the one number); income 23 is a blend of the 20/30 two-band schedule; capital gains 12% is the standard capital-income rate. Debt ~57.5% and revenue ~39.0% of GDP (Eurostat/OECD 2024). Spending is the general-government split scaled to expenditure near 43.5% of GDP.
